ai.description: This toad reaches 40–50 mm. It is brown or grey with dark mottling and a pale belly. Key features include a smooth, glandular skin and a lack of vomerine teeth.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Scutiger boulengeri* is best distinguished by the presence of distinct, prominent black spines on the chest and fingers of males, which are absent in other Indian *Scutiger*.
ai.habitat: *Scutiger boulengeri* inhabits high-altitude alpine meadows and rocky streams in the Himalayas, typically at elevations between 3,000 and 5,000 meters.
ai.behavior: The Xizang Alpine Toad is primarily nocturnal, emerging at night to forage for small invertebrates in the cold, high-altitude streams and rocky terrain of its habitat.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Scutiger boulengeri* breeds in high-altitude streams from June to August, laying small clutches of unpigmented eggs attached to stones in flowing water.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Scutiger boulengeri* is found in the high-altitude regions of the eastern Himalayas, specifically within the Indian state of Arunachal Pradesh at elevations above 3,000m.
ai.callDescription: The advertisement call of *Scutiger boulengeri* consists of a series of short, low-pitched, pulsed notes emitted by males from within cold, high-altitude mountain streams.
